title: Basic vs Deep Commercial Cleaning: What's the Difference and When Do You Need Each?
excerpt: Most businesses know they need 'cleaning' but can't tell you whether they need a standard daily clean or a deep clean — and they're paying for the wrong one. Here's the actual difference.
content:
## Two different jobs, often confused

A business owner rings a cleaning company and says "I need my office cleaned." The cleaner quotes for a standard daily clean. Three months later, the grout in the bathrooms is still discoloured, the kitchen extractor fan has a visible grease film, and the client wonders why the place still looks tired.

The cleaner isn't necessarily doing a bad job. They were doing the job they were asked to do. But the business needed a deep clean, not a standard clean — and no one clarified the difference at the start.

## What a standard commercial clean covers

A standard daily or regular commercial clean handles the day-to-day maintenance. It's the work that keeps a space looking presentable between more intensive interventions.

It includes:

- Vacuuming and mopping of floors
- Bathroom cleaning and sanitisation
- Kitchen and break room wipe-downs
- Rubbish removal and bin lining
- Surface dusting and wiping
- High-touch point cleaning (door handles, light switches)
- Reception and general area tidying

Standard cleaning is maintenance. It prevents things from deteriorating to the point of being noticeable. It doesn't fix things that have already deteriorated.

## What a deep clean actually means

A deep clean is a corrective intervention. It's the work that gets done to restore a space to a condition that regular maintenance alone can't achieve.

A proper deep clean includes:

- Carpet extraction and stain treatment
- Tile and grout scrubbing and restoration
- Oven, microwave, and kitchen appliance internals
- Extractor fan and range hood degreasing
- Skirting boards, vents, and high surfaces
- Behind and underneath furniture
- Sanitisation beyond surface level — full clinical-grade treatment in some environments
- Window blind cleaning
- Light fixture dusting

A deep clean takes significantly longer than a standard clean. A standard daily clean of a 200m² office might take 90 minutes. A deep clean of the same space could take a full day.

## When each applies

**You need standard cleaning** when your space is in generally good condition and you need day-to-day maintenance. This is the ongoing contract.

**You need a deep clean** in these situations:

- **Before a lease ends** — most commercial leases have a make-good clause requiring the space to be returned in a specific condition. A deep clean is usually part of that.
- **Post-construction** — after a fitout, there's construction dust and debris that no standard clean can handle. A post-construction clean is a specialist service on its own.
- **When surfaces have visibly deteriorated** — stained grout, carpet marks that vacuuming doesn't fix, kitchen surfaces with built-up grease. Standard cleaning won't touch these.
- **Seasonally, for high-traffic spaces** — in high-use commercial environments, a quarterly deep clean extends the life of carpets and floors and keeps the overall standard from drifting.
- **When a space has been unused** — if an office has been unoccupied for a period, a deep clean before reopening is standard practice.

## The cost difference

Deep cleaning is typically priced as a one-off project, not added to a regular contract. A one-off deep clean on a 300m² office might run $1,500–$3,500 depending on condition and scope. That's significant — but compared to the cost of carpet replacement or tile restoration that results from never deep cleaning, it's cheap.

Some cleaning companies include a deep clean in the contract as an annual or quarterly add-on. Others price it separately each time.

## One common mistake

Businesses that have never had a proper deep clean often don't know they need one. The standard clean keeps things tidy, and it seems fine — until a client points out the state of the grout in the bathroom, or you notice the carpet in the corner has changed colour.

A good cleaner will tell you when your space needs a deep clean. If yours never has, ask them to assess it. That's a reasonable question to put to any commercial cleaning provider in Newcastle.
